page_content:
[Context: This covers Overview1 where pituitary tumors are benign growths in the pituitary gland that alter hormone levels.]
Pituitary tumors are tumors that form in the pituitary gland near the brain.
These tumors can cause changes in hormone levels.
This illustration shows a smaller tumor, called a microadenoma.
Pituitary tumors are unusual growths that develop in the pituitary gland.
This gland is an organ about the size of a pea.
It's located behind the nose at the base of the brain.
Some of these tumors cause the pituitary gland to make too much of certain hormones that control important body functions.
Others can cause the pituitary gland to make too little of those hormones.
Most pituitary tumors are benign.
That means they are not cancer.
Another name for these noncancerous tumors is pituitary adenomas.

enrichments.context_summary: This covers Overview1 where pituitary tumors are benign growths in the pituitary gland that alter hormone levels.

page_content:
[Context: Treatment options for pituitary adenomas: surgery, medication, radiation, hormone management, or observation.]
Most adenomas stay in the pituitary gland or in the tissue around it, and they grow slowly.
They typically don't spread to other parts of the body.
Pituitary tumors can be treated in several ways.
The tumor may be removed with surgery.
Or its growth may be controlled with medications or radiation therapy.
Sometimes, hormone levels are managed with medicine.
Your health care provider may suggest a combination of these treatments.
In some cases, observation â€” also called a ''wait-and-see'' approach â€” may be the right choice.

enrichments.context_summary: Treatment options for pituitary adenomas: surgery, medication, radiation, hormone management, or observation.

page_content:
[Context: This covers Overview2 where pituitary adenomas are classified by hormone secretion, including ACTH, GH, and gonadotropins.]
Types of pituitary adenomas include:
Functioning.These adenomas make hormones.
They cause different symptoms depending on the kind of hormones they make.
Functioning pituitary adenomas fall into several categories, including those that make:Adrenocorticotropic hormone.This hormone also is known as ACTH.
These tumors are sometimes called corticotroph adenomas.Growth hormone.These tumors are called somatotroph adenomas.Luteinizing hormone and follicle-stimulating hormone.These hormones also are known as gonadotropins.

enrichments.context_summary: This covers Overview2 where pituitary adenomas are classified by hormone secretion, including ACTH, GH, and gonadotropins.

page_content:
[Context: Classification of pituitary adenomas by hormone type and size, noting pressure-induced symptoms.]
Pituitary tumors that make these hormones are called gonadotroph adenomas.Prolactin.These tumors are called prolactinomas or lactotroph adenomas.Thyroid-stimulating hormone.These tumors are called thyrotroph adenomas.; Nonfunctioning.These adenomas don't make hormones.
The symptoms they cause are related to the pressure their growth puts on the pituitary gland, nearby nerves and the brain.; Macroadenomas.These are larger adenomas.
They measure about 1 centimeter or more.
That's slightly less than a half-inch.
They can be functioning or nonfunctioning.; Microadenomas.These adenomas are smaller.
They measure less than 1 centimeter.
That's slightly less than a half-inch.
They can be functioning or nonfunctioning.

enrichments.context_summary: Classification of pituitary adenomas by hormone type and size, noting pressure-induced symptoms.

page_content:
[Context: This covers Overview where pituitary hormone-producing tumors are classified by hormone type and named accordingly.]
Adrenocorticotropic hormone.This hormone also is known as ACTH.
These tumors are sometimes called corticotroph adenomas.; Growth hormone.These tumors are called somatotroph adenomas.; Luteinizing hormone and follicle-stimulating hormone.These hormones also are known as gonadotropins.
Pituitary tumors that make these hormones are called gonadotroph adenomas.; Prolactin.These tumors are called prolactinomas or lactotroph adenomas.; Thyroid-stimulating hormone.These tumors are called thyrotroph adenomas.
Pituitary tumors are different from pituitary cysts.
A cyst is a sac that may be filled with air, fluid or other material.
A tumor is an unusual mass of cells that may grow over time.

enrichments.context_summary: This covers Overview where pituitary hormone-producing tumors are classified by hormone type and named accordingly.

page_content:
[Context: Cysts can develop adjacent to the pituitary gland, distinct from tumors or adenomas.]
Cysts may form on or near the pituitary gland, but they are not tumors or adenomas.

enrichments.context_summary: Cysts can develop adjacent to the pituitary gland, distinct from tumors or adenomas.

page_content:
[Context: Pituitary tumors may be asymptomatic or cause symptoms via mass effect or hormone imbalance, depending on size and hormone production.]
Not all pituitary tumors cause symptoms.
Sometimes these tumors are found during an imaging test, such as anMRIor aCTscan, that is done for another reason.
If they don't cause symptoms, pituitary tumors usually don't need treatment.
Pituitary tumor symptoms may be caused by a tumor putting pressure on the brain or on other parts of the body nearby.
Symptoms also can be caused by a hormone imbalance.
Hormone levels can rise when a pituitary tumor makes too much of one or more hormones.
Or a large tumor that disrupts the way the pituitary gland works may cause hormone levels to fall.

enrichments.context_summary: Pituitary tumors may be asymptomatic or cause symptoms via mass effect or hormone imbalance, depending on size and hormone production.

page_content:
[Context: This covers Symptoms where macroadenomas compress pituitary and nerves, causing headache, visual loss, facial pain, eyelid droop, seizures, nausea]
Macroadenomas can put pressure on the pituitary gland, on nerves, on the brain and on other parts of the body nearby.
That can cause symptoms such as:
Headache.; Eye problems due to pressure on the optic nerve, especially loss of side vision, also called peripheral vision, and double vision.; Pain in the face, sometimes including sinus pain or ear pain.; Drooping eyelid.; Seizures.; Nausea and vomiting.

enrichments.context_summary: This covers Symptoms where macroadenomas compress pituitary and nerves, causing headache, visual loss, facial pain, eyelid droop, seizures, nausea

page_content:
[Context: This covers Symptoms where functioning pituitary adenomas overproduce hormones or exert pressure, causing hormone-specific or mass effect symptoms.]
Functioning pituitary adenomas typically make a large amount of one hormone.
That exposes the body to high levels of that hormone.
Rarely, a pituitary adenoma may make more than one hormone.
The following types of functioning pituitary adenomas cause different symptoms depending on the hormones they make.
Luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) are also known as gonadotropins.
Pituitary tumors that make these hormones are called gonadotroph adenomas.
It's uncommon for these adenomas to make too many hormones that then trigger symptoms.
Instead, symptoms from these adenomas usually are due to tumor pressure.
If symptoms do happen because of too muchLHandFSH, they affect women and men differently.

enrichments.context_summary: This covers Symptoms where functioning pituitary adenomas overproduce hormones or exert pressure, causing hormone-specific or mass effect symptoms.

page_content:
[Context: This covers Symptoms where pituitary macroadenomas impair hormone production causing menstrual changes, and hormonal imbalances affect reproductive health.]
Symptoms in women may include:
Change in menstrual cycles.
Fertility problems.
Enlargement of and pain in the ovaries caused by a condition called ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome.
Symptoms in men may include:
Low testosterone levels (hypogonadism).
Reduced sperm count or fertility issues.
Macroadenomas can limit the pituitary gland's ability to make hormones.
When that happens, symptoms may include:
Tiredness or weakness.
Lack of energy.
Sexual problems, such as problems with erections and less interest in sex.
Changes in menstrual cycles.
Nausea.
Feeling cold.
Losing or gaining weight without trying.

enrichments.context_summary: This covers Symptoms where pituitary macroadenomas impair hormone production causing menstrual changes, and ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome leads to ovarian enlargement.

page_content:
[Context: This covers Symptoms where TSH‑secreting pituitary adenomas cause hyperthyroidism via excess T4, producing metabolic and neuro‑vegetative signs.]
Pituitary tumors that make thyroid-stimulating hormone are called thyrotroph adenomas.
They also may be referred to as thyroid-stimulating hormone-secreting tumors.
They cause the thyroid gland to make too much of the hormone thyroxine, also called T-4.
That leads to a condition called hyperthyroidism, also known as overactive thyroid disease.
Hyperthyroidism can speed up the body's metabolism causing many symptoms.
Some of the most common include:
Weight loss.; Rapid or irregular heartbeat.; Nervousness, anxiety or irritability.; Frequent bowel movements.; Sweating.; Tremor.; Sleep problems.
Symptoms of acromegaly include an enlarged face and hands.

enrichments.context_summary: This covers Symptoms where TSH‑secreting pituitary adenomas cause hyperthyroidism via excess T4, producing metabolic and neuro‑vegetative signs.

page_content:
[Context: This covers Symptoms where prolactinomas cause hyperprolactinemia, lowering sex hormones and producing menstrual, fertility, and sexual dysfunction.]
Changes to the face may cause the brow bone and lower jaw to jut out, and the nose and lips to get larger.
These adenomas are called prolactinomas.
Too much of the hormone prolactin can lead to a decrease in the body's levels of sex hormones â€” estrogen and testosterone.
Too much prolactin affects men and women differently.
In women, too much prolactin might cause:
Irregular menstrual cycles.; Lack of menstrual cycles.; Milky discharge from the breasts.; Breast tenderness.; Problems with fertility.; Less interest in sex.
In men, too much prolactin can cause a condition called male hypogonadism.
Symptoms might include:
Problems with erections.; Less interest in sex.; Breast growth.; Problems with fertility.; Less body and facial hair.

enrichments.context_summary: This covers Symptoms where prolactinomas cause hyperprolactinemia, lowering sex hormones and producing menstrual, fertility, and sexual dysfunction.

page_content:
[Context: This covers Symptoms where pituitary tumors cause hormone imbalance, treatable to restore levels, and hereditary MEN1 predisposes to such tumors.]
If you develop symptoms that might be associated with a pituitary tumor, see your health care provider.
Treatment for pituitary tumors often can bring hormones back to a healthy level and ease symptoms.
Although rare, some pituitary tumors are hereditary.
That means they run in families.
In particular, the hereditary disorder multiple endocrine neoplasia, type 1 (MEN 1) can cause pituitary tumors.
IfMEN 1runs in your family, talk to your health care provider about tests that may help find a pituitary tumor early.

enrichments.context_summary: This covers Symptoms where pituitary tumors cause hormone imbalance, treatable to restore levels, and hereditary MEN1 predisposes to such tumors.

page_content:
[Context: This covers Causes where pituitary tumor etiology is largely unknown, with rare inherited genetic causes.]
The pituitary gland and the hypothalamus are in the brain.
They make hormones that control many important functions in the body.
The pituitary gland is a small organ about the size of a pea.
It's located behind the nose at the base of the brain.
Despite its small size, the pituitary gland has an effect on nearly every part of the body.
The hormones it makes control important body functions, such as growth, blood pressure and reproduction.
The cause of uncontrolled cell growth in the pituitary gland, which creates a tumor, remains unknown.
In rare cases, pituitary tumors can be caused by genes you've inherited.
But most have no clear hereditary cause.

enrichments.context_summary: This covers Causes where pituitary tumor etiology is largely unknown, with rare inherited genetic causes.

page_content:
[Context: This covers Causes where genetic alterations may contribute to pituitary tumor development.]
But most have no clear hereditary cause.
Still, scientists think that changes in genes may play an important role in how pituitary tumors develop.

enrichments.context_summary: This covers Causes where genetic alterations may contribute to pituitary tumor development.

page_content:
[Context: This covers Risk factors where hereditary conditions (MEN1, MEN4, Carney, McCune-Albright) are the only known risk factors for pituitary tumors.]
Most people who get pituitary tumors don't have any factors that put them at higher risk of developing these tumors.
Environment and lifestyle choices don't seem to have an effect on a person's risk of pituitary tumors.
Although genetics seems to play a role, most people who have pituitary tumors don't have a family history of them.
The only known risk factors are several rare hereditary conditions that raise the risk of many health problems, including pituitary tumors.
These conditions include:
Multiple endocrine neoplasia, type 1, also called MEN 1.; Multiple endocrine neoplasia, type 4, also called MEN 4.; Carney complex.; McCune-Albright syndrome.

enrichments.context_summary: This covers Risk factors where hereditary conditions (MEN1, MEN4, Carney, McCune-Albright) are the only known risk factors for pituitary tumors.

page_content:
[Context: This covers Complications where pituitary tumors cause visual loss, hypertension, hyperglycemia, osteoporosis, cardiac issues, and cognitive deficits.]
Pituitary tumors usually don't spread to other parts of the body.
They can affect a person's health, though.
Pituitary tumors may cause:
Problems with eyesight, including vision loss.; High blood pressure.; High blood sugar.; Bone loss.; Heart problems.; Problems with thinking and memory.

enrichments.context_summary: This covers Complications where pituitary tumors cause visual loss, hypertension, hyperglycemia, osteoporosis, cardiac issues, and cognitive deficits.

page_content:
[Context: This covers Complications where pituitary tumor compression of medial temporal lobe causes focal seizures with impaired awareness.]
If a pituitary tumor presses on part of the brain called the medial temporal lobe, it may lead to a seizure.
This type of seizure is known as a focal seizure with impaired awareness.
These seizures involve a change in or loss of consciousness or awareness.
If you have one of these seizures, you may seem to be awake.
But you stare into space and don't respond as you typically would to the environment around you.
You may not remember the seizure after it happens.

enrichments.context_summary: This covers Complications where pituitary tumor compression of medial temporal lobe causes focal seizures with impaired awareness.

page_content:
[Context: This covers Complications where pituitary tumor removal causes permanent hormone deficiency requiring lifelong replacement therapy.]
Having a pituitary tumor or having one removed with surgery may permanently change your body's hormone supply.
As a result, you may need hormone replacement therapy for the rest of your life.

enrichments.context_summary: This covers Complications where pituitary tumor removal causes permanent hormone deficiency requiring lifelong replacement therapy.

page_content:
[Context: Pituitary apoplexy: sudden tumor hemorrhage causing severe headache, visual loss, nausea, confusion, treated emergently with steroids and surgery.]
A rare but potentially serious complication of a pituitary tumor is pituitary apoplexy.
This happens when there is sudden bleeding into the tumor.
Symptoms include:
A severe headache, likely worse than you've ever had before.; Problems with your eyesight, including double vision or loss of vision in one or both eyes.; Nausea and vomiting.; Confusion or other reduced mental function.
Pituitary apoplexy requires emergency treatment.
The treatment usually includes taking corticosteroid medicine to ease swelling around the tumor.
You also may need surgery to remove the tumor.

enrichments.context_summary: Pituitary apoplexy: sudden tumor hemorrhage causing severe headache, visual loss, nausea, confusion, treated emergently with steroids and surgery.

page_content:
[Context: This covers Diagnosis where blood tests and CT/MRI imaging detect pituitary adenoma.]
Blood tests.Blood tests can show whether your body has too much or too little of certain hormones.
For some hormones, blood test results that show too much of the hormone may be all that's needed for your health care provider to diagnose a pituitary adenoma.
CTscan.A computed tomography scan, also called aCTscan, is a type of imaging test that combines a series of X-rays to create cross-sectional images.MRIscans are used more often thanCTscans to detect and diagnose pituitary tumors.
But aCTscan may be helpful in planning surgery if your health care provider tells you that a pituitary tumor must be removed.
For other hormones, such as cortisol, a blood test result that shows too much of the hormone may need to be followed by other tests.

enrichments.context_summary: This covers Diagnosis where blood tests and CT/MRI imaging detect pituitary adenoma.

page_content:
[Context: This covers Diagnosis where MRI imaging detects pituitary tumors, revealing size, location, and hormone activity.]
Those tests can show if the earlier result was caused by a pituitary adenoma or by another health concern.
MRIscan.A magnetic resonance imaging scan, also called anMRIscan, is a test that uses a magnetic field and computer-generated radio waves to create detailed images of the body's organs and tissues.
AnMRIof the brain can help detect a pituitary tumor and show its location and size.
Pituitary tumors often aren't noticed or aren't detected.
In many cases, that's because the symptoms caused by pituitary tumors that make hormones, called functioning adenomas, and large tumors, called macroadenomas, are similar to those of other medical conditions.
It's also because they grow very slowly over time.

enrichments.context_summary: This covers Diagnosis where MRI imaging detects pituitary tumors, revealing size, location, and hormone activity.

page_content:
[Context: This covers Diagnosis where nonfunctioning pituitary microadenomas are incidentally detected via imaging and hormone testing.]
Small pituitary tumors that don't make hormones, called nonfunctioning microadenomas, often don't cause symptoms.
If they are detected, it's typically because of an imaging exam, such as anMRIor aCTscan, that's done for another reason.
Results that show hormone levels are too low need to be followed with other tests, usually imaging exams, to see if a pituitary adenoma may be the cause of those test results.
To detect and diagnose a pituitary tumor, your health care provider will likely talk with you about your personal and family medical history and do a physical exam.
Testing to detect a pituitary tumor also may include:
Urine tests.A urine test may be used to help diagnose a pituitary adenoma that's making too much of the hormoneACTH.

enrichments.context_summary: This covers Diagnosis where nonfunctioning pituitary microadenomas are incidentally detected via imaging and hormone testing.

page_content:
[Context: This covers Diagnosis where excess ACTH causes Cushing disease and vision testing detects pituitary tumor effects.]
Too muchACTHleads to too much cortisol in the body and causes Cushing disease.
Vision testing.A pituitary tumor can affect eyesight, especially side vision, also called peripheral vision.
Testing your eyes to check how well you can see may help your health care provider decide if other tests may be needed to detect a pituitary tumor.
Your health care provider may refer you to a specialist in hormone disorders, called an endocrinologist, for more testing.

enrichments.context_summary: This covers Diagnosis where excess ACTH causes Cushing disease and vision testing detects pituitary tumor effects.

page_content:
[Context: This covers Treatment where pituitary adenoma management uses surgery, medication, or radiation with a multidisciplinary team.]
Avoid more damage to the pituitary gland and restore its regular function.
Brain surgeon, also called a neurosurgeon.
Hormone disorder specialist, also called an endocrinologist.
If a pituitary adenoma needs treatment, it may include surgery to remove the tumor.
Medication or radiation therapy also might be used to treat a pituitary adenoma.
Treatment involves a team of medical experts.
The team may include a:
Many pituitary adenomas don't need treatment.
They are not cancer, so if they don't cause symptoms, simply watching them over time may be a good approach.
If treatment is needed, the specific treatment depends on the tumor type, size, location and growth over time.

enrichments.context_summary: This covers Treatment where pituitary adenoma management uses surgery, medication, or radiation with a multidisciplinary team.

page_content:
[Context: This covers Treatment where hormone imbalance from pituitary tumors is corrected by surgery, radiation, and hormone normalization.]
If a tumor is causing too much or too little of certain hormones in the body, that also affects the treatment.
Your age and overall health play a role in treatment planning too.
Nose and sinus surgeon, also called anENTsurgeon.
Radiation therapy specialist, also called a radiation oncologist.
Return hormone levels to a healthy range.
Reverse symptoms caused by tumor pressure or prevent them from getting worse.
The goal of treatment is to:

enrichments.context_summary: This covers Treatment where hormone imbalance from pituitary tumors is corrected by surgery, radiation, and hormone normalization.

page_content:
[Context: This covers Treatment where surgical resection of pituitary adenoma relieves hormone excess, pressure, and visual deficits.]
Causes other symptoms, such as headache or facial pain.
Causes the body to make too much of some hormones.
Lowers hormone levels in the body due to pressure on the pituitary gland.
Presses on the optic nerves and limits eyesight.
Results after surgery typically depend on the adenoma type, its size and location, and whether the tumor has grown into tissues around it.
Surgeries to remove a pituitary tumor include endoscopic transnasal transsphenoidal surgery and craniotomy.
Surgery to treat a pituitary tumor involves removing the tumor.
This is sometimes called a tumor resection.
A surgeon may suggest surgery if a pituitary adenoma:

enrichments.context_summary: This covers Treatment where surgical resection of pituitary adenoma relieves hormone excess, pressure, and visual deficits.

page_content:
[Context: This covers Treatment where transnasal transsphenoidal endoscopic surgery removes pituitary adenomas without external incisions.]
During the surgery, a surgeon â€” typically a neurosurgeon partnering with a nose and sinus surgeon â€” removes the adenoma through the nose and sinuses.
The surgery doesn't require an external cut, also called an incision.
It does not affect other parts of the brain.
The surgery doesn't cause a scar that you can see.
In transnasal transsphenoidal endoscopic surgery, a surgical instrument is placed through the nostril and alongside the nasal septum to access a pituitary tumor.
Large macroadenomas may be hard to remove with this surgery.
That's particularly true if a macroadenoma has spread to nearby nerves, blood vessels or other parts of the brain.
This surgery also is called adenomectomy.

enrichments.context_summary: This covers Treatment where transnasal transsphenoidal endoscopic surgery removes pituitary adenomas without external incisions.

page_content:
[Context: This covers Treatment where adenomectomy removes pituitary adenoma.]
This surgery also is called adenomectomy.
It's the most common surgery used to remove a pituitary adenoma.

enrichments.context_summary: This covers Treatment where adenomectomy removes pituitary adenoma.

page_content:
[Context: This covers Treatment where transcranial surgery, also called a craniotomy, is used less often than transnasal surgery for pituitary tumors.]
Transcranial surgery also is called a craniotomy.
It is used less often than endoscopic transnasal transsphenoidal surgery for pituitary tumors.
Bleeding.
Brain injury.
Damage to the pituitary gland.
Double vision or loss of vision.
Transcranial surgery and transnasal surgery are generally safe procedures, but complications can include infection, reaction to anesthesia, and temporary headache.

enrichments.context_summary: This covers Treatment where transcranial surgery (craniotomy) details and general surgical risks are described.

page_content:
[Context: This covers Treatment where transcranial surgery removes large macroadenomas via an upper skull scalp incision for better access and visualization.]
This surgery makes it easier to reach and remove large macroadenomas or pituitary tumors that have spread to nearby nerves or brain tissue.
It also makes it easier for the surgeon to see the extent of the tumor, as well as the parts of the brain around it.
During transcranial surgery, the surgeon removes the tumor through the upper part of the skull through a cut in the scalp.

enrichments.context_summary: This covers Treatment where transcranial surgery removes large macroadenomas via an upper skull scalp incision for better access and visualization.

page_content:
[Context: This covers Treatment where pituitary tumor surgery can damage the gland, causing diabetes insipidus via vasopressin loss.]
If your health care provider suggests surgery to treat a pituitary tumor, ask about which surgery is right for you.
Talk about the possible complications, risks and side effects.
Ask what you can expect during recovery.
Surgery to remove a pituitary tumor might damage the pituitary gland.
That can limit its ability to make hormones, leading to other medical problems including diabetes insipidus.
This condition happens when the pituitary gland cannot make enough of the hormone vasopressin.
That hormone is made in the back of the gland, an area called the posterior pituitary.
Diabetes insipidus causes the body's fluids to go out of balance, which then causes the body to make large amounts of urine.

enrichments.context_summary: This covers Treatment where pituitary tumor surgery can damage the gland, causing diabetes insipidus via vasopressin loss.

page_content:
[Context: This covers Treatment where diabetes insipidus after pituitary tumor removal is managed with vasopressin.]
That can cause extreme thirst and raise the risk of dehydration.
Diabetes insipidus after surgery to remove a pituitary tumor usually is short term.
It typically goes away without treatment within a few days.
If diabetes insipidus lasts longer than that, treatment with a manufactured form of vasopressin may be used.
The condition often goes away after several weeks or months.

enrichments.context_summary: This covers Treatment where diabetes insipidus after pituitary tumor removal is managed with vasopressin.

page_content:
[Context: This covers Treatment where radiation therapy for pituitary adenomas is evaluated, with delayed benefits, side effects, and long-term follow-up.]
A radiation oncologist evaluates your condition and talks with you about the benefits and risks of radiation therapy for your situation.
It usually takes months to years to see the maximum benefit of radiation therapy for pituitary adenomas.
Side effects and complications from radiation therapy usually don't show up right away either.
It is important to have regular long-term follow-up care to detect any hormone problems that may happen due to radiation therapy.
Causes symptoms that medications don't relieve.
Comes back after surgery.
Damage to healthy tissue near the pituitary gland.
Damage to other nerves close to the pituitary gland.
Damage to the pituitary gland that limits its ability to make hormones.

enrichments.context_summary: This covers Treatment where radiation therapy for pituitary adenomas is evaluated, with delayed benefits, side effects, and long-term follow-up.

page_content:
[Context: This covers Treatment where external beam radiation and IMRT deliver fractionated, shaped doses to pituitary tumors, reducing side effects.]
External beam radiation.This method also is called fractionated radiation therapy.
It delivers radiation in small amounts over time.
A series of treatments usually is done five times a week for 4 to 6 weeks.
Intensity modulated radiation therapy.This type of radiation therapy, also called IMRT, uses a computer that allows the beams to be shaped to surround the tumor from many angles.
The strength of the beams can be limited.
That lowers the risk of side effects on healthy tissue.
Isn't completely removed with surgery.
Methods of radiation therapy that can be used to treat pituitary tumors include:
Potential side effects and complications of radiation therapy for pituitary adenomas can include:

enrichments.context_summary: This covers Treatment where external beam radiation and IMRT deliver fractionated, shaped doses to pituitary tumors, reducing side effects.

page_content:
[Context: This covers Treatment where proton beam therapy targets pituitary adenomas, delivering energy precisely to reduce healthy tissue damage.]
Proton beam therapy.Another radiation option, proton beam therapy uses positively charged ions, called protons, to target tumors.
Proton beams stop after releasing their energy within the tumor.
This means the beams can be controlled to target a pituitary adenoma with less risk of side effects in healthy tissue.
This type of radiation therapy requires special equipment.
It isn't widely available.
Radiation therapy can be helpful if a pituitary tumor:
Radiation therapy uses high-energy sources of radiation to treat pituitary tumors.
Radiation therapy can be used after surgery.
Or it can be used alone if surgery isn't an option.
Slightly increased risk of developing a brain tumor.

enrichments.context_summary: This covers Treatment where proton beam therapy targets pituitary adenomas, delivering energy precisely to reduce healthy tissue damage.

page_content:
[Context: Stereotactic radiosurgery for pituitary adenomas: precise, single high-dose radiation with imaging guidance, minimal healthy tissue exposure, aims to control growth or hormone secretion]
Stereotactic radiosurgery.Often delivered as a single high dose, this type of radiation therapy precisely focuses radiation beams on the tumor.
Although the word "surgery" is in its name, no cut into the skin is needed.
It delivers radiation beams the size and shape of the tumor into the tumor with the aid of brain-imaging techniques.
This requires attaching a head frame to the skull.
The frame is removed right after treatment.
Little radiation comes in contact with healthy tissue near the tumor.
That lowers the risk of damage to the healthy tissue.
The goal of radiation therapy for pituitary adenomas is to control adenoma growth or to stop the adenoma from making hormones.
Vision changes due to damage to the optic nerves.

enrichments.context_summary: Stereotactic radiosurgery for pituitary adenomas: precise, single high-dose radiation with imaging guidance, minimal healthy tissue exposure, aims to control growth or hormone secretion

page_content:
[Context: This covers Treatment where medications lower hormone production and shrink pituitary adenomas.]
Treatment with medications can be useful for the management of pituitary adenomas.
They can help lower the amount of hormones the body makes due to a tumor.
Some medications also can shrink certain types of pituitary tumors.

enrichments.context_summary: This covers Treatment where medications lower hormone production and shrink pituitary adenomas.

Mifepristone doesn't lower the amount of cortisol the body makes.
Instead, it blocks the effects of cortisol on the body's tissues.

[Context: Oral octreotide (Mycapssa) treats GH‑secreting pituitary adenomas post‑surgery, mimicking injections, may worsen diabetes.]
A form of octreotide that can be taken in a pill, called Mycapssa, also is available.
It works like the forms that are given as a shot and has similar side effects.
Two kinds of medication can treat pituitary tumors that make growth hormone.
Providers often prescribe these medications when surgery to remove a pituitary adenoma hasn't worked to return the amount of growth hormone in the body to a healthy level.

page_content:
[Context: This covers Treatment where hormone replacement therapy restores hormone levels after pituitary adenoma or its treatment causes deficiencies.]
The pituitary gland controls growth, thyroid function, adrenal function, reproductive function and the balance of water in the body.
One or all of those can be harmed by a pituitary adenoma or by its treatment with surgery or radiation.
This is because of the hormone changes they can cause.
If your hormones fall to unhealthy levels, you may need to take hormone replacement therapy.
This can restore hormones to a healthy level.

[Context: This covers Treatment where watchful waiting monitors pituitary adenoma growth and hormone changes.]
In watchful waiting â€” also known as observation, expectant therapy or deferred therapy â€” you might need regular follow-up tests to see if a tumor grows or if hormone levels change.
Watchful waiting may be a choice for you if an adenoma isn't causing any symptoms or triggering other health problems.
Talk to your health care provider about the benefits and risks of watchful waiting versus treatment in your situation.

page_content:
[Context: This covers Coping and support where patients are encouraged to educate themselves, share feelings, and seek support groups.]
It's natural for you to have questions throughout the diagnosis and treatment of a pituitary tumor.
The process can be overwhelming and sometimes scary.
That's why it's important to learn as much as you can about your condition.
The more you know and understand about your care, the better.
You might find it helpful to share your feelings with other people who are in a situation like yours.
Check to see if support groups for people with pituitary tumors are available in your area.
Hospitals often sponsor these groups.
Your health care provider may be able to help you find the emotional support you need.
